Identity: a northern logging camp in a spruce clearing, on a rutted logging road. Two buildings and a working yard:
a long LOG BUNKHOUSE (bunkroom + cook-and-mess hall, loft over) of dark bark-on spruce logs with saddle-notched
corners whose log ends stick out, a cobblestone plinth, a steep grey slate-shingle gable roof, a covered front porch

road, with a louvred monitor on its ridge and a red-brick boiler stack trailing a tall plume. A log deck of
bark-on logs feeds the mill from the road; behind it the yard of pale sawn lumber in stickered stacks; a woodshed
lean-to behind the bunkhouse; stumps everywhere, standing spruces only at the edges.

1. `plinthCourse(x0,z0,x1,z1,y)`: ring of `cobblestone` at the edge of the box; `mossy_cobblestone` at 1 in 6, always at the four corners.
2. `logCourse(x0,x1,y,z,axis)`: a straight run of `spruce_log` with `axis`, skipping cells that are opening cells (callers pass a skip list).
3. `saddleNotch(x,y,z,axis)`: one protruding log end, `spruce_log` with the wall's axis, placed one past the corner per FACADES parity.
4. `porchBay(x0,x1)`: porch deck planks z=5..7, `stripped_spruce_log` post(s) y=2..3 at z=5, `spruce_fence` y=2 between posts.

7. `doorPair(x,y,z,facing,hinge)`: `spruce_door` lower and upper, same `facing` and `hinge`, door faces out of the room it closes.

input.summary:
Sawmill pole frame built in parts/sawmill.mjs: plank floor y=0 (x 23..35, z 8..20), 12 stripped posts y=1..5, top plate y=6, ring-placed knee braces, west half walls, south back boards with lintel and 3x3 doorway, and the saw carriage (rails, log, stonecutter at 29,1,14).
make.sh finished with a whole build.nbt; the part placed 375 blocks with no REFUSED writes and no OFF-PALETTE blocks. Gables, monitor and loft door are left to the roof and fittings parts.
check: no floating or unsupported blocks in the mill; the 15 orphans it reports are all bunkhouse log ends (part 1). Front and zoomed north renders show the open frame and carriage as planned.

waste.what: Floor of the mill written cell by cell with a nested x/z loop of g.set
waste.tool: A g.fill-style call that works on the runParts view (or a vocab floor(x0,z0,x1,z1,block) helper) would replace the loop.

waste.what: Knee brace positions worked out by hand: ring-neighbour test for each post and its four directions, plus the facing toward each post
waste.cost: about 20 minutes of reasoning, one retry-free build
waste.tool: kneeBrace-along-edge helper, e.g. braceEdge(g, x0,z0,x1,z1, postList, y) that places one brace per free edge cell beside every post and faces it.

waste.what: Lintel over the doorway placed by a g.set loop because boardBay would otherwise fill y=4
waste.cost: 3 set calls and the ordering trick (lintel before boardBay)
waste.tool: boardBay option for a lintel row, or a doorway box that carries its header through the wall.

waste.what: Checking the tiles by eye, then a second zoom render to confirm the braces and carriage
waste.tool: mcd zoom with a --radius and a check that lists which cells of a named box are air, so placement is confirmed without reading an image.

companions.task: Build and fit the saw carriage and its rails at x=28 and x=30 (rails, log, stonecutter at 29,1,14) and confirm the carriage runs clear of the doorway lane.
Check the post and plate joints and the knee braces on the north and long sides before the roof's gable planks go on.

left: The north-front and east-side braces and posts are open by design; the roof tool and the fittings part fill the gables, monitor, sign and loft door.
The bunkhouse part (P1) leaves 15 orphan log ends at x=3..4 and x=18..19; they are its cells, not mine, and I did not touch them.
The roof part's cottage roof wrote polished_deepslate stairs and slabs that are off the palette (roof.json, P3); not my part.
